authoredPrompt: This figure illustrates the AlexNet convolutional neural network architecture using a 3D volume diagram viewed in perspective. A left-to-right flow begins with a sheared input photograph representing the 224×224×3 input image, followed by a sequence of three-dimensional feature map volumes rendered as parallelogram-faced blocks in light teal (#d3edeb) for the main face and darker teal (#a0d9d3) for the depth layers, while orange (#d18362) and dark orange (#773c23) parallelogram blocks represent convolutional filter kernels applied at each stage. The feature map volumes progressively shrink in spatial resolution while increasing in depth, with labeled dimensions 55×55×96, 27×27×256, and 13×13×384 corresponding to the first three convolutional stages of AlexNet. Ellipsis (…) markers appear within the teal volume stacks to indicate that only a representative subset of the channels is depicted. A “Conv 5×5” annotation above one inter-stage region identifies the kernel size of one convolution, and black arrows with arrowheads indicate the forward data flow between stages. This figure introduces the AlexNet architecture, showing how successive convolution and pooling operations reduce spatial resolution while extracting increasingly abstract feature representations.
authoredInteractions:
- Animate data flow: sequentially highlight each 3D tensor block from input 224×224×3 through 55×55×96 and 27×27×256 to 13×13×384, displaying the spatial dimensions shrinking and channel depth growing at each conv/pool step
- Slider for layer index (1–3): select a convolutional stage, highlight its tensor block, and show an overlay with the Conv 5×5 kernel size and the resulting feature map dimensions
- Drag to rotate a selected tensor block: inspect how the depth (channel) dimension grows relative to the shrinking spatial height and width across AlexNet's early layers

discrepancies: The convolutional stages are misrepresented as teal output tensors preceded by separate orange kernel blocks, while the source shows the main convolution/pooling layer blocks themselves as orange/brown cuboids.
The later 13×13×256 stages before the FC columns are missing or collapsed into floating labels and extra small kernel cubes instead of distinct orange cuboids.
The FC layers are shorter segmented teal stacks with small dots, whereas the source has tall cyan broken columns with clear jagged gaps and dotted ellipses.

Several labels do not match the source exactly, including the visible typo-like 'Copy 11×11' instead of 'Conv 11×11', and the operation labels are not arranged with the same slanted textbook callout style.
The input image is a simplified geometric candle scene rather than a close visual match to the source photograph panel.
The yellow inspection overlay and highlighted tensor add clutter not present in the original figure.
evaluation.notes: The overall AlexNet left-to-right pipeline is recognizable, but the layer semantics, colors, missing 13×13×256 blocks, and FC proportions differ substantially from the source.
action_items: Replace the teal convolution output blocks and extra orange kernel blocks with the source-like orange/brown cuboids representing each network stage.
Add the missing distinct 13×13×256 cuboids before the FC section and place their dimension labels directly above them.
Make the FC columns taller with jagged break marks and dotted ellipses matching the reference.
Correct label text and placement, especially 'Conv 11×11 Stride 4', and use slanted callout arrows closer to the textbook figure.
plan_action_items: Revise the plan to model the source as a static full AlexNet architecture diagram rather than a kernel-inspection diagram with extra separate filter blocks.
Use an orthographic/axonometric textbook-style projection instead of a perspective 3D camera if the goal is visual fidelity to the reference.
